Daughter’s dengue deteriorated rapidly without warning signs, physician parents realise too late
item.description:
Whenever patients sought advice on dengue, physician Muhammad Omar Faruq Raihan would instruct them to monitor closely for red flags: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or bleeding in vomit and stool. Yet, when his own daughter, Famiya Mashnur Rumaisa, contracted the virus, none of these typical warning signs manifested. Before her parents could even register that her condition was turning critical, the young girl passed away.

Famiya Mashnur was 8 years, 10 months, and 14 days old. She was a Class-III (English version) student at the Banasree branch of Ideal School in the capital. Her fever spiked on the morning of 29 September; within three days, on the afternoon of 1 October, she breathed her last.

Muhammad Omar Faruq Raihan works as an anaesthesia and ICU specialist at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery. His wife, Farzana Sultana, is an ophthalmologist at Vision Eye Hospital in Dhaka. Famiya was the couple’s elder daughter.

She had meticulously planned her upcoming birthday on 17 November—a trip to Cox’s Bazar to cut a cake and spend quality time with her parents and younger sister. She went shopping with her mother and bought matching outfits for herself and her younger sister.

“After she was found dengue positive in a test, there was no sign whatsoever that her condition was deteriorating,” physician Omar Faruq told Prothom Alo. “We simply couldn’t gauge it. Upon reaching Square Hospital, she couldn’t even survive half an hour in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) before passing away.”

The physician couple’s younger daughter, Farjin Mahnur Warisa, aged 5 years and 8 months, was constantly attached to her elder sister, who often bathed and took care of her. Unaware of the permanence of death, Farjin has been told that her sister—whom she affectionately called ‘Iya’—has gone to God, and she has processed the loss in her own innocent way.

Omar Faruq and Farzana Sultana recounted that on the night of Sunday, 27 September, Famiya complained of feeling feverish. Her temperature rose the following morning, preventing her from attending school. On Tuesday, diagnostic tests confirmed she was dengue-positive. An intravenous cannula was inserted at home to administer saline. As Omar Faruq had to travel outside Dhaka for urgent professional duties, no further blood tests were performed on Wednesday.

On Thursday morning, Famiya mentioned feeling unwell. Soon after, she suffered a sudden seizure and was rushed to a local hospital in Banasree. Lacking PICU facilities, she had to be transferred across the city to Square Hospital. Traffic delays compounded the critical situation; by the time they reached Square Hospital, her condition had severely worsened, and she began bleeding from her nose. Shortly after, she succumbed to the illness. Prior to this rapid decline, she had been alert, conversing with family members, and drinking coconut water sent by her grandmother.

Her mother, Farzana Sultana, now paces through their home, surrounded by memories of a daughter who loved organising her keepsakes. The grieving parents are attempting to find solace in the thought that her lifespan was destined to be short. Heartbreaking regrets linger—the girl had asked for mango juice the day before her death but could not drink it, and her birthday dress remains untouched in the wardrobe.

They cannot bring themselves to forget such memories: at this time last year, the whole family travelled together for Hajj, while the daughter took her last selfie with her parents and sister during a trip to Sajek in July.

Omar Faruq recalled his daughter’s sensitive nature, noting how she felt embarrassed when her mother changed her clothes in front of a domestic worker after a bout of vomiting.

He added that Famiya’s mother had also contracted dengue shortly before Famiya fell ill, but recovered with home care and IV saline. Unfortunately, those same interventions proved ineffective for their daughter.

Omar Faruq Raihan reflected that the outcome might have been different if adequate PICU facilities were available across hospitals, if public healthcare services were more robust, and if local authorities had initiated effective Aedes mosquito control measures ahead of the dengue season.

Pointing to an open waste dump near his Banasree residence where stagnant water accumulates, he noted that urban sanitation oversight remains severely neglected.

A specialist who daily treats severely burned children at the Burn Institute, Omar Faruq Raihan admitted he was always terrified that his daughter might hurt herself in the kitchen and repeatedly urged her to stay away from it. “In the end,” the grieving father lamented, “she suffered and died from the bite of a tiny mosquito.”

item.title: Lawyers scuffle at court over bail hearing of Maj (retd) Akhtaruzzaman
item.description:
During the hearing of Major (Retd.) Akhtaruzzaman’s bail application, BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami supporting lawyers got involved in an uproar and altercation in the presence of the judge.

This incident took place on Sunday afternoon in the court of Magistrate Jamshed Alam at Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Court.

During the tension between the two groups of lawyers, the judge entered his chamber but later returned to conduct the hearing. Even then, there were arguments and scuffles between the BNP and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers.

Following the unexpected situation in the courtroom, as Akhtaruzzaman was being brought down from the court building after the hearing, BNP and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers again engaged in a scuffle. Each side blamed the other for the incident.

Akhtaruzzaman was arrested by police on Friday last in a case regarding chaos at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka over a luggage and trolley crisis, obstruction to government work, and the accusation of assaulting an official.

After a one-day remand, he was presented in court on Sunday afternoon. The police sought an order to send him to jail, while Akhtaruzzaman’s lawyer applied for his bail.

Major (Retd.) Akhtaruzzaman, who was elected a Member of Parliament twice from BNP, joined Jamaat-e-Islami last December ahead of the 13th National Election.

A group of Jamaat-affiliated lawyers represented him in court today. Before the judge arrived at the bench, a dispute arose in the courtroom over space between pro-BNP lawyers and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers, leading to chaos and shoving between the two groups.

In this situation, the judge came to the bench at 2: 41 PM. Even after his arrival, the lawyers didn’t stop. The judge left the bench and went back to his chamber. When the situation calmed down a bit, the judge returned to the bench at 2: 45 PM.

At that time, Akhtaruzzaman, standing in the dock with his hand raised, requested permission from the judge, saying, "Ten lawyers will argue on my behalf. I am requesting permission for all ten to be heard."

During the hearing, there was again loud arguing and exchange of words between the two sides' lawyers in the presence of the judge.

Filing the application to keep Akhtaruzzaman detained in jail, the investigation officer of the case, Sub-Inspector Majedul Islam of the Airport Police Station, stated, during interrogation, the accused admitted to the truth of the incident and provided some information.

The obtained information from the accused is being verified. The investigation is ongoing comprehensively. In this situation, for the sake of a fair and unbiased investigation, it is imperative to keep the accused detained until the investigation is complete.

In the hearing, Akhtaruzzaman’s lawyer Abdur Razzak told the court, he (Akhtaruzzaman) is a former major and a several-time member of parliament. The allegations against him are false. This court granted permission for his interrogation yesterday. Today, after the remand, he has been brought to court. The allegation related to the airport incident is not his crime. As a conscious citizen, he has protested.

This lawyer argued that injustice and wrongdoing were done to Akhtaruzzaman at the airport, claiming many others also suffered from this hardship. Some of these incidents have been seen in videos on Facebook.

The conduct for which the case was filed was essentially his act of protest. Is protesting against injustice and wrongdoing a crime for a conscious citizen and a freedom fighter? As a freedom fighter, member of parliament, and former major, where everyone honours and respects him, injustice was done to him at the airport.

Claiming that Akhtaruzzaman was arrested for political reasons, his lawyer further told the court, "He is ill, suffering from various ailments. We are requesting his bail on any conditions. The sections submitted in the case are eligible for bail. We are requesting bail."

Meanwhile, another lawyer for the defence, Saifur Rahman, also applied for Akhtaruzzaman's bail.

Opposing the bail, the state lawyer Omar Farooq Farooqi told the court, "We have seen a video. In that, it seems this accused is behaving very badly at the airport. He is throwing items haphasardly. Protest is not a crime, but the language of protest should be like a protest. He did not protest there; he committed a crime. Assaulting someone can never be an expression of protest."

PP Omar Farooq further stated, "BNP has given birth to many leaders in this country. They forget after taking advantage. There are many such opportunists. They survived on our resources."

At this point, Jamaat-affiliated lawyers became agitated and protested. Akhtaruzzaman, standing in the accused dock, was seen smiling while looking at the PP and shaking his head to indicate 'no'.

The PP told the court, there can never be bail in this case. It is very necessary to know what power and support are behind such behaviour, for the sake of investigation. If the accused is granted bail, it will obstruct the investigation.

Protesting the prosecutor's statement, the defence lawyer Abdur Razzak said, "Yesterday, the PP called the accused 'discarded goods'. This cannot be a hearing. We protest."

At this stage of the hearing, at 3: 08 PM, lawyers of BNP and Jamaat-affiliated groups again caused an uproar. The judge then instructed them to stop.

At that time, the defence lawyers argued, "Considering age, physical condition, and illness, we are seeking the accused’s bail. This is a bailable case. He deserves bail." Objecting to this statement, the PP said, "Akhtaruzzaman has sided with the fascists and participated in illegal elections. He spoke against the July movement. To save himself after that, he joined Jamaat who have also sheltered him to give us slander. Jamaat fosters some people just for abusing the government, for questioning the government's development."

After hearing arguments from both sides, the court rejected the bail and ordered Akhtaruzzaman to be sent to jail.

After the court’s order, police, under strict security, escorted Akhtaruzzaman down the stairs. However, upon reaching the first floor, a noise and scuffle of BNP and Jamaat-affiliated lawyers were reported below the court building, and Akhtaruzzaman was held there for a moment.

At that time, BNP-supporting lawyers tried to disperse the Jamaat-affiliated lawyers and their supporters protesting below the court building. Both sides then got into a shoving and scuffling. Later, when police brought the situation under control, Akhtaruzzaman was brought down.

Later, in a briefing, the state's lawyer Omar Farooq Farooqi stated, "Jamaat wants to create mobs everywhere. That day, Akhtaruzzaman created a mob at the airport. Today, Jamaat's lawyers and their supporters from outside created a mob. Their intention is to worsen the situation by creating mobs. From the morning, I have seen them gathering. They had filled the courtroom beforehand."

On the other hand, Akhtaruzzaman's lawyer Abdur Razzak said, "What do they mean by outside people? We didn’t bring any outsiders. If every of the 35,000 lawyers have one client each, that makes 35,000 clients. What they are saying is not correct at all."

item.title: Finance minister: Capital market to be transformed within a year
item.description:
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury Sunday said the face of Bangladesh's capital market will change completely within the next year, with the market becoming far stronger.
"If there is no accident and the capital market keeps running the way it is now, a huge positive change will come in the market within the next year," Khasru said at World Investor Week 2026, organized by the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (BSEC) at Khamarbari in the capital.
The minister said the capital market is in a much better position than in the past and investors are regaining confidence.
He added that many large foreign companies have also shown interest in investing in Bangladesh's stock market.
"I was not confident about how I could approach big foreign companies with the capital market in this state. But when I talked to them, they expressed interest. They are constantly keeping track of Bangladesh. They trust the current leadership of Bangladesh. They will come to the Bangladesh market soon," he said.
Urging everyone to stop dwelling on past events in the capital market and move forward, Khasru said: "If we want integrity and transparency, we must become self-regulated. Every institution, including brokers, exchanges, investors and financial entities, must play the role of a self-regulator. I do not believe in regulatory bodies."
Stressing the need to bring the capital market into the broader economic ecosystem, he said the NBR, Bangladesh Bank and the capital market had so far worked like isolated islands. "Now we have built an ecosystem where everyone will work together."
The minister also warned that businesses relying on high-interest bank loans will not survive competition.
He said the government and private institutions alike tend to borrow from banks at high interest rates at the slightest need, an approach that cannot sustain businesses in the global market.
"Money must be raised from the market, and the best avenue for that is the capital market. We are also working to strengthen the bond market," he said.
Khasru said Bangladesh can never become a trillion-dollar economy by 2034 by borrowing from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
"I have cancelled my meeting with the IMF. I have told them plainly that the government is not bound to accept their conditions. We need $50 billion every year. How much will the IMF give us? And then we would have to accept conditions again. All that is out from now on. We will raise money from the market and do business," he said.
Saying the government will not finance the business needs of state enterprises, the minister said: "Why should the government pay to buy aircraft? It cannot be that the government provides taxpayers' money and enterprises do business with it."
He said the country's financial architecture is being overhauled and the economy will become market-based in the days ahead.
The depth of the shallow capital market will be increased to make the economy more market-oriented, he added.

item.title: UK envoy discusses broader ties, trade and investment with PM
item.description:
British High Commissioner to Bangladesh Sarah Cook on Sunday met Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and discussed the overall state of Bangladesh-UK relations, including prospects for greater trade and investment, economic cooperation and human resource development.
The meeting was held at the Prime Minister’s Office in the Cabinet Division of Bangladesh Secretariat, said a press release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
During the meeting, they exchanged views on various issues of bilateral relations and matters of mutual interest.
They stressed the importance of further strengthening and broadening the longstanding and friendly relations between Bangladesh and the UK.
The two sides also discussed expanding cooperation in education, skills development and migration.
Tarique and the British envoy exchanged views on continued UK support for Bangladesh’s economic development and progress, as well as the prospects for further expanding trade and investment between the two countries in the future.
They expressed optimism about taking the existing friendly relations between Bangladesh and the UK forward and exploring new areas of cooperation for mutual benefit.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir and officials concerned were present.

item.title: Food influencers sell taste, but what about the health risks?
item.description:
Food vloggers and content creators are growing rapidly in Dhaka and across Bangladesh as videos about cheap meals, huge portions, and street food often go viral, and sometimes hundreds of viewers try out the places they see online.
But as these creators influence what people eat, an important question comes up: when they promote a dish, do they tell viewers about its nutrition, health risks, or how hygienically it is prepared?
Videos that show “more food at a lower price” are especially popular.
A food shop in Agargaon offered beef and rice for Tk100, chicken and rice for Tk80, and egg and rice for Tk60, all with unlimited rice and curry.
After a YouTube video about the shop went viral, about 400 people started visiting every day.
These kinds of videos are everywhere on social media platforms.
Another video showed Tk99 basmati biryani and Tk130 kacchi in Mirpur 10, while another featured Tk120 basmati kacchi in Mirpur 12.
In July 2026, another food vlogger highlighted Tk99 basmati rice chicken biryani and Tk130 beef biryani in Mirpur 10.
These videos mainly attract viewers with their prices, big portions, and the eating experience.
But when people decide to try the food, it’s important to ask if they should also get basic information about the ingredients or any health concerns.
Dr Tasnim Sanowar, chief quality control officer at the Institute of Public Health, said: “Food content usually focuses on taste, price and portion size. But there is very little discussion about the possible health effects of eating certain foods regularly.”
“When a food is presented attractively on social media, and such content influences people's food choices, providing at least relevant health information should be considered. This does not mean turning food bloggers into doctors. Rather, it means ensuring the information consumers need to make their own decisions.”
Recent studies show that food content on social media is more than just entertainment.
For example, a 2025 review in BMJ Global Health examined 36 studies on how social media and online food marketing affect children and teenagers.
Most of the research so far has focused on high-income countries, and the researchers say more studies are needed in low- and middle-income countries.
Another study looked at 8,871 videos from top TikTok influencers in the US.
Out of these, 1,360 videos featured food, drinks, or dietary supplements.
The study found that 58% of the foods shown were considered unhealthy.
Some creators agree that health information belongs in food content.
Mir Raihan Masud of "Raihanism Travel & Food" said bloggers should tell viewers about the possible health risks of the food they review.
“They should definitely do that. It can help people become more aware of what they eat. Many people in Bangladesh suffer from diet-related diseases such as heart disease and diabetes. Since food bloggers can reach a large number of people, they also have a responsibility,” he said.
Mir, a former BBC Bangla journalist who recently became a food blogger, added that bloggers should mention whether a food contains too much salt, sugar, or oil.
He said: “People like useful information. If correct information is presented in a nice and simple way, it will not make the content less attractive.”
Food and nutrition specialist Dr Farzana Wahab said the word “healthy” must be used carefully.
“Calling a food tasty or good for its price is not the same as calling it ‘healthy’. If the word healthy is used, it should be based on nutrition science. A food content creator can talk about the taste or experience of eating a food, but it is important to verify whether they are providing nutritional or medical information,” she said.
Dr Farzana added: “There is no need to put a large warning on every food item. But if it is reliably known that a food contains excessive salt, sugar or oil, this can be explained to viewers in simple language. This does not mean banning the food. It simply means providing people with information.”
Nasrin Akter, assistant director of the investigation branch at the Directorate of National Consumers' Right Protection, spoke about food and restaurant promotion and said: “Consumers should know whether that information is advertising or an independent opinion. This is particularly important in influencer marketing. The clearer this line is, the greater the opportunity for consumers to make an informed choice.”
Dhaka University fourth-year student Mukta Akter said: “Sometimes I feel like trying a food after watching a food blogger's video, especially when the price is low and the food looks good. But it would be helpful if the video also said what is in the food or whether there is anything people should keep in mind if they eat it regularly, instead of talking only about the taste and price. Not everything needs a warning, but if you provide important information, we can make more informed decisions.”

item.title: President: Free, fair polls, space for opposition essential for democracy
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Sunday said democracy is a culture that is built gradually through regular practice, stressing the need for free, fair and impartial elections as well as adequate space for the opposition and political rivals to make democracy effective.
“Democracy is a culture that develops step by step through regular practice. Free, fair and impartial elections are essential for this,” he said.
The President made the remarks when a delegation led by Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr ABM Obaidul Islam paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban.
President's Press Secretary Md Sarwar Alam briefed reporters after the meeting.
The president also stressed the need to provide adequate space to the opposition and political rivals to make democracy effective.
“That is the beauty of democracy. Democracy must be allowed to function effectively in its own course,” he said.
Referring to Dhaka University, Mirza Fakhrul said the country's premier university is not only a leading center of education but also a focal point of Bangladesh's politics, history, heritage and culture.
He called for further improving the quality of education at the university and taking it to the level of the world's leading universities.
During the meeting, the Vice-Chancellor congratulated Mirza Fakhrul on his election as President and briefed him on the university's overall academic activities.
VC Obaidul Islam invited the president, in his capacity as Chancellor of Dhaka University, to attend the university's upcoming 54th convocation.
The president accepted the invitation and assured the delegation that he would attend the convocation.
The president's military secretary, secretary and press secretary, and Dhaka University's pro-vice-chancellor and treasurer were present at the meeting.

item.title: Shama Obaed: Bangladesh expects India to show political intent on Hasina extradition
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Sunday said Bangladesh expects India to expedite the ongoing extradition process to bring back accused individuals, including convicted ex-prime minister Sheikh Hasina, as swiftly as possible, stressing that political intent is equally important alongside legal procedures.
“While legal procedures must be respected, political intent is equally crucial. We expect the Indian government to expedite the ongoing extradition process to bring back the accused individuals as swiftly as possible,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs when her attention was drawn over Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi’s comments.
Shama said it is entirely possible to extradite the accused under the framework of the extradition treaty, and that legal process is actively being pursued.
"To give you a straight answer, again and again, the government of India, through the Spokesperson at the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), has replied to this that there is a process, and the process involves legality, and it is well structured. So, as far as that is concerned, the process is on,” Trivedi said on Saturday.
The courts are involved in the matter and therefore “nobody can give you a timeframe,” he said at a discussion titled “Power and Prudence: Managing Great-Power Competition without Conflict” as part of the ongoing Bay of Bengal Conversation in Dhaka.
The Indian High Commissioner highlighted the need for continuous dialogue, mutual respect and trust between the two countries to address bilateral issues, saying every issue between the two neighbors has a solution.
“There’s no point hiding the issues, and there’s no point not talking about the issues,” he said.
Trivedi, who faced a couple of questions, said the two countries need to discuss all outstanding issues, including water, trade, culture, sports, communication and transportation, through appropriate forums.
“In a democracy, the dialogue has to be there at the proper forum. And the dialogue has to be a continuous dialogue,” he said, noting that the process of engagement between the two countries may be slow, but it has not stopped.
“I can guarantee you, there is no stoppage of process. The process is ongoing,” Trivedi said. “Believe me, there has to be a solution, and there will be a solution,” the Indian diplomat added.

item.title: Heightened security planned at 781 Durga Puja mandaps in Faridpur
item.description:
Extensive security measures have been taken at 781 puja mandaps in Faridpur ahead of Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community.
The authorities have directed the organisers to install CCTV cameras, ensure adequate lighting and deploy volunteers at each venue.
The directives were issued at a meeting held at the conference room of the Faridpur deputy commissioner on Sunday with Deputy Commissioner Mazharul Islam in the chair.
Members of Puja Udjapon Committees, senior officials of government agencies and civil society representatives were present at the meeting and discussed the issues of security, law and order, traffic management and idol immersion arrangements at the puja venues.
The puja mandaps will be categorised based on security risks, with security arrangements strengthened accordingly.
Police, Ansar and Village Defence Party (VDP) members will be deployed at the puja venues while plainclothes police and intelligence personnel will also remain on duty.
Shahriar Mohammad Miaji, Superintendent of Faridpur Police, said the district police have made all-out preparations to ensure that Durga Puja is celebrated in a safe and peaceful environment while maintaining communal harmony and mutual goodwill.
Deputy Commissioner Mazharul Islam said the administration has taken all necessary measures to ensure peaceful and uninterrupted celebrations. He urged people to maintain tolerance, harmony and goodwill during the festival.
The authorities also instructed the organisers to strictly follow the designated schedules and routes for idol immersion. They advised against playing drums or other musical instruments at high volume during Maghrib and Isha prayer times in order to maintain religious harmony.
The district police’s cybercrime monitoring cell will remain active round the clock to prevent attempts to disrupt communal harmony through rumours, misleading information or provocative posts on social media.
People have been advised to contact the national emergency service 999 or the Faridpur Police Control Room in case of any emergency.

item.title: 12kg LPG cylinder price rises to Tk 1,837
item.description:
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised the price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), setting the price of a 12kg cylinder at Tk 1,837, up from Tk 1,585.
The new price, an increase of Tk 252, will take effect from 6:00pm on Sunday.
The regulator has also raised the price of autogas, used in vehicles, to Tk 84.62 per litre from Tk 73.09.
The price hike comes amid a severe LPG shortage in the market and allegations that cylinders were being sold at inflated prices. Some had claimed the shortage was artificial, while others argued that a price increase would help restore normal supplies.
BERC said the latest adjustment was made in response to higher international LPG prices, shipping costs and diesel prices used for transportation.
Consumers had reported difficulties finding LPG cylinders in the two weeks before the new price was announced, although traders denied any shortage.
In September, there were also allegations that 12kg cylinders, officially priced at Tk 1,585, were being sold for Tk 2,200 to Tk 2,500.
It remains to be seen whether LPG supplies will return to normal following the price hike.

item.title: ULAB celebrates 23rd foundation day with grand festivities, cultural performances
item.description:
ULAB celebrated its 23rd Foundation Day on Sunday at the ULAB Campus under the theme "Celebrating 23 Years of Building Capability."
The daylong celebration brought together distinguished guests, faculty members, students, alumni, and members of the ULAB community to mark more than two decades of academic excellence, innovation, creativity, and community engagement.
Throughout the day, the campus featured five interactive zones-Discover, Develop, Demonstrate, Distinguish, and Belong- showcasing ULAB's academic opportunities, experiential learning, student achievements, creativity, and vibrant club activities.
The celebration also featured student capability showcases, global cultural and embassy engagements, the "Ideas of Bangladesh" wall, international partnership exhibitions, Chinese calligraphy by the Confucius Institute, and Japanese cultural activities, including a yukata dress-up and origami workshop hosted by the Japanese Embassy.
The formal celebration ceremony began at 4pm with the ULAB Theme Song, followed by welcome remarks from Professor Shamsad Mortuza, PhD, vice chancellor of ULAB.
In his remarks, he highlighted ULAB's 23-year journey and its commitment to quality education, innovation, and building future-ready graduates. A video presentation showcasing the university's achievements and milestones was also screened.
Addressing the gathering, Kazi Anis Ahmed, PhD, president of the ULAB Board of Trustees, emphasized that creativity, independent thinking, and academic excellence remain central to ULAB's founding vision and educational philosophy.
AKM Tareq, deputy managing director of Mutual Trust Bank PLC, joined as the special guest.
He highlighted the importance of practical skills, leadership, and industry-academia collaboration in preparing graduates for the future.
Professor Milan Kumar Bhattacharjee, PhD, special advisor to the Board of Trustees and Treasurer of ULAB, highlighted the university's institutional progress, innovation, and future aspirations.
The ceremony also featured a crest handover and the cutting of the 23rd anniversary cake. Professor Dr Jude William R Genilo, pro vice chancellor of ULAB, delivered the vote of thanks, expressing gratitude to the guests, organizers, faculty members, students, alumni, and all contributors to the celebration
The daylong festivities concluded with a grand concert featuring a headline performance by the popular Bangladeshi rock band WARFAZE, bringing the university's 23rd Foundation Day celebration to a vibrant close.

item.title: Baridhara crash: Court rejects teen’s bail plea
item.description:
A Dhaka court has rejected the bail petition of the 17-year-old boy accused in the death of construction worker Mehedi Hasan Mim in a car crash in Baridhara, with the judge saying his continued detention could send a “positive message” to children.
Dhaka Juvenile Court-8 Judge Md Abdul Moktadir passed the order on Sunday after hearing the bail petition.
“The boy’s release at the earliest stage would send a negative message to society. But keeping him detained could send a positive message to children,” the judge said.
State counsel Mohammad Sharif Uddin Mamun confirmed the bail rejection.
The case concerns the death of 24-year-old Mehedi, who was sitting on a footpath on Road 1 in Baridhara Diplomatic Zone around 5pm on September 22 when a speeding private car lost control and ran him over. He was taken to Kurmitola General Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
People at the scene detained a teenager who was in the driver’s seat and handed him over to police. Police released him into his uncle’s custody later that night after questioning.
Mehedi’s brother Moktadir Islam filed a case with Gulshan police on September 23, naming Akash Mark as the accused driver but not naming the teenager.
Following criticism over his release, police took the teenager into custody the same day and produced him before court on September 24, seeking his detention at the Child Development Centre in Gazipur.
The teenager’s lawyers later sought bail, saying the victim’s family had reached a Tk9 lakh settlement.
During Sunday’s hearing, defence lawyer Md Golam Mostofa Khan argued that the teenager was not driving the car and had only been inside it. He also cited the settlement between the families.
The state opposed bail, saying the case was serious and that the teenager was involved in the incident while the car was being driven recklessly. The prosecution also said he did not have a driving licence.
The judge referred to CCTV footage that allegedly showed the teenager getting out from the driver’s side and said police had found preliminary evidence of his involvement.
The judge also said releasing him could create the impression that someone could drive recklessly, cause an accident and still secure bail quickly.
The court subsequently rejected the bail petition.

item.title: Indians protest election chief as police probe harassment claims
item.description:
Indians rallied for a third day on Sunday demanding the election commission chief's resignation, while police launched an investigation into sexual harassment allegations against officers during protests in New Delhi a day earlier.
Protests began on Friday demanding the Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down, alleging wrongdoing during a large-scale voter-roll revision that has removed millions of names from the lists.
The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing. Kumar himself has not commented.
Thousands marched in Mumbai on Sunday, waving Indian flags, demanding Kumar step down.
Protesters have included supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) -- which began in May as a satirical online movement, and succeeded in its campaign to oust the then education minister.
"Mumbai is out on the streets again for free and fair elections!" CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post on Sunday.
"Solidarity with all the protestors," he added. "All Indians need to come together. It's now or never!"
In New Delhi, a few dozen activists, including CJP supporters, gathered outside a police station on Sunday to demand action over the allegations against officers during protests in the capital on Saturday.
The harassment allegations were made after police detained scores of protesters around the government-designated protest site of Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
"Allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers," Delhi police said in a statement, promising "a fair and impartial enquiry".
In a video posted on social media, a complainant said that a police officer pushed and touched her "inappropriately".
CJP activist Saurav Das, in a post on social media, said that "a delegation with the victim is inside the police station".
Dipke said that the accused officer "must be arrested immediately".
Opposition politicians have accused the ECI of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
They have said they will march to the Election Commission in New Delhi on Tuesday, and hold "Save Democracy" rallies countrywide afterwards.
The CJP has called for a "massive mobilisation of young Indians" in New Delhi on October 10.

item.title: ICT sets Oct 6 to complete testimony in Ziaul Ahsan case
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has set October 6 to complete the testimony of the investigation officer in the crimes against humanity case against Major General (retd) Ziaul Ahsan over allegations of enforced disappearance and killing of more than 100 people during the Awami League government.
Tribunal-1 passed the order on Sunday following a prosecution petition. Earlier, investigation officer Md Rafiqul Islam gave partial testimony on September 30.
The prosecution said three charges had been brought against Ziaul Ahsan following a lengthy investigation. A formal charge was filed against him on December 17, 2025, and the tribunal framed charges and ordered the trial to begin on January 14, 2026.
Ziaul Ahsan served as director general of the National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre (NTMC). He was arrested in mid-August 2024.
The prosecution said the state’s presentation of evidence would conclude with the completion of the investigation officer’s testimony. The defence will then have an opportunity to present its evidence, followed by the arguments stage.
Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim had earlier said the prosecution believed it had established the charges against Ziaul Ahsan through the testimony of 15 witnesses.

item.title: Mahfuz Anam: Groups that dismantle autocracy become each other’s enemies
item.description:
The Daily Star Editor and Publisher Mahfuz Anam said groups that unite to dismantle an autocratic system eventually become each other’s enemies, causing repeated failures to institutionalize democracy in Bangladesh.
He made the remarks on Sunday, on the second day of the three-day Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026, organized by the Centre for Governance Studies (CGS), at the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel in Karwan Bazar, Dhaka.
Mahfuz Anam said: “In the past, instead of institutionalizing free and fair elections, we increasingly fell into conflict, competition and then destruction, and I think we failed because we really do not know how to run our country. We actually do not know what governance is. We really do not know how to bring together a people with all their strength, all their innovation, all their resilience and turn that source into national development.”
“In my view, one reason is that the nation becomes united while dismantling a dictatorship, but once the dictatorship is dismantled, the nation becomes divided. The groups that work together to destroy the dictatorship become each other’s enemies, and that is where we have repeatedly, repeatedly and repeatedly failed to institutionalize the rebuilding of democracy in Bangladesh.”
Mahfuz Anam said Bangladesh had an almost endless capacity to fail to build democracy after dismantling autocratic systems.
“Unfortunately, we have an almost endless capacity that we cannot build democracy after dismantling autocracy. We were born again as Bangladesh, which was against a very brutal military dictatorship, but we failed to build a democratic Bangladesh and then there was a military coup. Ershad fell and we returned to democracy in 1991, and we really hoped that this would be the rebirth of democracy in Bangladesh, and we had several elections under a caretaker government.”
“However, and in my view the reason is that in Bangladesh we have over-politicized every institution imaginable.”
He said: “Doctors are divided over which political party you belong to. They are divided in many other professions, including journalism. You have pro-BNP journalists, you have pro-Jamaat journalists. I mean, how can a journalist be pro-politics? I mean, you can have a personal preference and of course you are free to vote, but in a profession where credibility is your life responsibility, how can you publicly support a political party and still expect to enjoy credibility?”
Mahfuz Anam said excessive politicization had eroded the functioning of almost all institutions.
“So we have a system where excessive politicization in one way has eroded the functioning of almost all our institutions. You really run a country through an efficient bureaucracy. We have been politicized. The police are always used as a partisan extension of your party. Muscle power and intelligence agencies are again used for political purposes.”
“So constitutional bodies such as the Anti-Corruption Commission and the Information Commission, these bodies which are considered constitutional bodies and are independently operated, are all politicized. So, to cut a long story short, the truth is that we are so good at destroying autocracy, but the sad reality is that we are so bad at building democratic institutions.”
Mahfuz Anam said the main problem was excessive politicization, which had caused the entire governance system to fail.
“So when a party is elected through the democratic process, we celebrate the expression of the people’s will. But very soon we realize that the outcome of that election result is transformed into political reality instead of public interest.”
“Obviously, it is worldwide that every political party, whether the Labor Party wins in England, or the Democrats or Republicans win in the United States, there will be some partisanship. But turning your entire governance system into an extension of your own party is where the decline begins, and one of the first consequences is corruption.”
“One of its first consequences is nepotism and partisan favoritism. Day after day, month after month and year after year, our entire governance system collapses.”
He said modern technology had made governance a science.
“Now with modern technology, governance is a science. Governance is not just good wishes and dreaming a dream. Governance is how you translate that dream. Technology can now give us a highly efficient bureaucracy and an efficient police force and, at the same time, a fair police force.”
“And here I think Bangladesh now faces its biggest challenge, if we want to move forward. Because by definition Bangladesh is a country where governance is not easy. We have a small land area. We have a huge population. We have natural challenges, but we have enormous potential if we can turn our human resources into a valuable productive asset, which we can do through technology, education and good governance.”

item.title: Ahmed Shaheen joins Mercantile Bank as AMD
item.description:
Renowned banker Ahmed Shaheen has joined Mercantile Bank PLC as additional managing director (AMD).
Prior to his new role, he served as additional managing director at Eastern Bank PLC (EBL), where he drove significant advancements in the bank.
With a distinguished career spanning over 33 years in the Bangladesh banking industry, Ahmed Shaheen is widely recognized as a strategic leader and a pioneer in financial product innovation.
He began his banking journey in late 1992 as a probationary officer at IFIC Bank.
Over the years, he has successfully steered critical verticals, including international banking, corporate relationship units, and structured finance.
He also brought his expertise to Prime Bank Limited as deputy managing director and chief business officer from 2015 to 2016.
Ahmed Shaheen is a graduate of the University of Dhaka and did his post-graduation from AIUB.
He holds the Certified Documentary Credit Specialist (CDCS) certification from the Institute of Financial Services, UK, and he is also a certified graduate in Finance of International Trade.
He works as a member of the Banking Commission of ICC Bangladesh.
Throughout his career, he played an instrumental role in bringing impactful changes in the banking industry especially in trade finance.
He’s joined Mercantile Bank as the bank pursues institutional modernization, comprehensive digital transformation, and robust risk governance.
The bank expresses strong optimism that under his executive leadership, Mercantile Bank will expand its sustainable finance portfolio, optimize asset quality, and introduce cutting-edge financial services for corporate and retail customers alike.

item.title: Community Bank launches BO account opening facility on Community Cash App
item.description:
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC has introduced a new facility on its digital banking platform, Community Cash, enabling customers to apply for opening Beneficiary Owner (BO) accounts directly through the app.
The new facility is expected to make the process of accessing investment opportunities in Bangladesh’s capital market more convenient, faster and easier for the bank’s customers.
Under the new digital service, Community Bank customers can initiate their application for opening a BO account through the Community Cash app.
Community Bank Investment Limited (CBIL), a wholly owned subsidiary of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, will subsequently facilitate the BO account opening process.
CBIL is engaged in the bank’s investment banking and capital market-related activities.
By bringing banking and investment-related services together through a digital platform, the initiative is aimed at making the entry process into the capital market more accessible for customers.
Those interested in investing in the capital market will be able to initiate the BO account opening process through the Community Cash app with greater ease and convenience.
The new feature was formally inaugurated by Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, managing director of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC. and director of Community Bank Investment Limited.
Senior officials of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC and Community Bank Investment Limited were present at the occasion.

item.title: Savor International wins ‘Best Mice Initiative 2026’ award
item.description:
Savor International Limited has received the “Best Mice Initiative 2026” award at the Bangladesh Tourism Award 2026, organized by the Bangladesh Tourism Board.
The award ceremony was held at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center, Agargaon, Dhaka.
The recognition was awarded to Renex 2026 – Renewable Energy Exhibition, a key part of the 11th edition of Safecon.
Focusing on renewable energy, clean energy, solar technology and energy storage, RENEX serves as a specialized business platform connecting local and international companies, technology providers, investors and industry professionals.
At the ceremony, M Rashiduzzaman Millat, Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism, handed over the award to KM Ferdous Ilias, deputy general manager, and Umma Rokeya Nisha, AGM, on behalf of Savor International Limited.
The “Best Mice Initiative 2026” award marks an important recognition of Savor International Limited’s contribution to Bangladesh’s Mice (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions) industry.
Through its international exhibitions and business platforms, Savor continues to connect Bangladesh’s industries with global markets, technologies and investment opportunities.

item.title: Pubali Bank, United Healthcare to launch credit card, banking product sales campaign
item.description:
Pubali Bank PLC and United Healthcare Services Ltd. recently inaugurated a Credit Card and other banking products sales campaign.
On the occasion, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was also signed between the two organizations to strengthen collaboration and provide enhanced banking benefits and services to customers.
Md Shahnewaz Khan, deputy managing director of Pubali Bank PLC, and Mohammad Faizur Rahman, chief executive officer of United Healthcare Services Ltd, were present at the event.
Under the campaign, all doctors and staff of United Healthcare will receive complimentary credit cards along with other banking benefits from Pubali Bank PLC.
The event was also attended by Abu Raihan Al Beruni, chief financial officer; Subroto Kumer Shuvo, assistant general manager; and Tareq Sami Rahman, lead for corporate affairs of United Healthcare Services Ltd.
From Pubali Bank PLC, Sukanta Chandra Banik, general manager & head of Gulshan corporate branch; NM Firoz Kamal, deputy general manager & head of card business division; Md Abu Nasar, deputy general manager & advance in charge Gulshan corporate branch; Mossabbir Hossain Talukder, assistant general manager & head of card sales; and Md Ashadulla Khan, assistant general manager & head of card marketing were present, along with other senior officials of both organizations.
Under the agreement, all Pubali Cardholders can enjoy up to 20% discount on pathological & radiological tests at United Healthcare.

item.title: Grameen HealthTech champion under ‘Inclusion & Community Services’ in BIIN Awards 2026
item.description:
Shukhee, the AI-enabled, patient-centric and interoperable digital healthcare application and community-care ecosystem developed by Grameen HealthTech Limited, has won the Bangladesh ICT & Innovation Network (BIIN) Awards in the "Inclusion & Community Services" category for delivering affordable and continuous healthcare to rural and underserved communities.
Held on October 3 at Brac University Auditorium, the award was received on behalf of Grameen HealthTech by CEO Dr Ahmed Arman Siddiqui; chief business and technology officer Mohammad Solaimun Russell; strategic adviser Mohammad Abul Hossain Bangabashi; chief marketing officer Kingshuk Haque; application tech lead Md Tanvir Hossain; and chief of research, analytics, and customer experience Dr Hossain Md. Al-Amin.
Expressing gratitude to the BIIN organizers and jury board, partner organizations, and the Grameen Group family, Grameen HealthTech CEO Dr Ahmed Armaan Siddiqui said in a statement to the media: "This recognition belongs to every Link Worker, doctor and service recipient who has made Shukhee a part of their lives. Healthcare should not depend on where a person lives. This award will inspire us to bring quality healthcare to every household in Bangladesh."
Shukhee is designed to deliver affordable, accessible and continuous healthcare, particularly for rural, underserved and digitally excluded communities.
It connects patients, doctors, pharmacies, diagnostic centres, hospitals, caregivers, Shukhee Seba Kendro and community-based Shukhee Link Workers through one integrated care pathway.
Its services include 24/7 telemedicine, specialist consultations, digital prescriptions, medicine delivery, home diagnostics, referrals, mental-health support, maternal and child healthcare, and NCD management.
Continuous follow-up is supported by integrated, interoperable Electronic Medical Records (EMR).
An AI-enabled healthcare chatbot provides 24/7 service navigation, preliminary symptom intake, health education, appointment assistance, and medication and follow-up reminders, with seamless escalation to qualified healthcare professionals.
The Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) draws on structured patient histories, clinical observations and real-time vital signs to help doctors identify risk and make guideline-based, evidence-informed decisions.
Through doorstep Link Workers, Shukhee Seba Kendro and connected medical devices, including the Shukhee Sastho Bondhu 6-in-1 Device for real-time health assessment, Shukhee turns every rural household into a connected point of patient-centric care.

item.title: LPG price hike adds to consumer woes amid supply shortages
item.description:
Consumers are growing worried over the latest LPG price hike as shortages persist across the country, with 12-kg cylinders being sold for Tk 2,200 to Tk 2,500 in areas where gas is available, far above the newly announced official price of Tk 1,837.
Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) on Sunday announced a fresh hike in Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices at the consumer level, raising the rate of a 12-kilogram cylinder by Tk 252 to Tk 1,837.
However, field reports indicate that consumers across the country are already trapped in a chaotic retail market where 12-kg cylinders are selling for between Tk 2,200 and Tk 2,600—up to Tk 1,000 above government-fixed benchmarks—while many retail outlets have run completely out of stock.
While state-owned LP Gas Limited (LPGL) maintains a price of Tk 777 for its 12.5-kg cylinder, its negligible market share leaves over 98 percent of the country’s bottled gas consumers entirely dependent on private distributors.
The price hike comes just a day after Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood and Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir held an urgent meeting with LPG importers at Secretariat on Saturday to address the deteriorating market situation.
The high-level intervention follows the Energy Minister’s September 30 directive to Deputy Commissioners (DCs) to investigate whether an artificial crisis is being engineered by market syndicates and to take strict legal action against price gougers.
Industry insiders and energy experts attribute the unprecedented supply strain to a severe shortfall in national pipeline natural gas.
According to Petrobangla, against a nationwide demand of nearly 4,000 million cubic feet per day (MMCFD), current domestic extraction and LNG regasification deliver only around 2,600 MMCFD.
The resulting power cuts and pipeline gas shortages have forced thousands of households, commercial eateries, and small industries to shift to bottled LPG, creating a demand surge that existing private distribution networks are struggling to meet.
Compounding local issues, private importers cite mounting international headwinds.
For September, Saudi Aramco raised its Contract Price (Saudi CP) to $625 per ton for propane and $660 per ton for butane.
More critically, global LPG availability has tightened due to Middle East geopolitical conflicts, driving ocean freight rates to record highs.
Importers said while BERC calculated retail prices using a freight benchmark of $160 per ton, actual international shipping costs have surged to $400 per ton, forcing several private operators to curtail import volumes to prevent heavy financial losses.
The market crisis has also triggered internal friction within the LPG sector.
Official reports indicate that LPG imports dropped from nearly 160,000 tons in August to around 120,000 tons in September.
However, a group of LPG operators submitted a formal letter to the Energy Division on October 1 claiming import volumes remained steady.
They alleged that certain major importers deliberately delayed offloading and releasing imported LPG cargoes to generate artificial market pressure and inflate prices, demanding an independent inquiry into the bottleneck.
With winter approaching—a season that traditionally sees a seasonal uptick in global heating fuel demand—consumers and industry stakeholders warn that without strict market monitoring and streamlined import support, Bangladesh’s LPG market could face even deeper instability in the coming months.
Denouncing the price hike, Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB) Energy Adviser Prof M Shamsul Alam termed BERC's decision a "validation of illegal market manipulation."
He said the raising official prices while failing to enforce retail compliance only shields dishonest syndicates without ensuring gas availability for ordinary citizens.
Energy expert and former BUET professor Dr Ijaz Hossain highlighted the policy oversight behind the crisis, emphasizing that shifting the nation's energy demand from depleted domestic pipeline gas to imported LPG without expanding state-owned buffer stocks or establishing a price stabilization fund leaves consumers at the mercy of private cartels and volatile global freight markets.

item.title: Deputy speaker urges accountability for failure to enforce child laws
item.description:
Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal on Sunday stressed the need to ensure proper enforcement of laws to protect children's rights by holding those responsible accountable in case of failure.
“In cases of domestic violence where children are subjected to abuse and exploitation, law enforcement agencies unfortunately become compromised. There is a lack of scrutiny (monitoring) in our country regarding the extent to which executive officials are actually fulfilling their responsibilities,” he said.
The deputy speaker made these remarks at a dialogue titled "What Can We Do to Eliminate Child Labour" arranged by Action for Social Development (ASD) at the KIB Complex in the capital.
Citing that the ministers and MPs are elected for a particular period, while the executive officials remain in charge for a long time, he said the government officials must be held accountable in case of failure to enforce laws.
“Why are we not bringing government officials within the ambit of accountability? They receive their salaries from taxpayers’ money and must be accountable for their responsibilities,” he said.
Talking about child rape, Barrister Kayser Kamal said, unfortunately, this has turned into a social disease. “Why? Because they (children) are the most vulnerable elements and also the worst victims in our society,” he said.
He put emphasis on raising public awareness to overcome this social problem. “If we wish to overcome this situation, the first thing we need is public awareness. The government has a helpline—1098—though many of us may not be aware of it. Why isn't the number 1038 on everyone's lips today? While 999 is widely known, why isn't 1098?
The Deputy Speaker said 12-13% of the 1,400 people killed during the 2024 July Uprising were children.
He called for stronger coordination among Parliament, relevant Ministries, law enforcement agencies and NGOs working on child labour and child rights.
He urged the authorities concerned to ensure that existing laws and government projects related to child protection are properly implemented, saying that laws alone are not enough to protect child rights.
The Deputy Speaker urged participants to pledge not to employ children aged below 14 as domestic workers, saying efforts to eliminate child labour must begin from one's own home. “Let us start from this very room,” he said.

item.title: Plan International Bangladesh highlights youth access to climate finance
item.description:
Plan International Bangladesh organized a high-level dialogue titled “From Climate Finance to Youth Action: Access, Opportunities and Barriers for Young People” as part of the Regional Conference of Youth – Asia and the Pacific (RCOY APAC) 2026 at BRAC University in Dhaka on Sunday.
The event brought together senior government officials, diplomatic representatives, climate finance institutions, development practitioners and young climate leaders to examine challenges preventing young people from accessing climate finance and translating their ideas into sustainable climate solutions.
The dialogue highlighted a disconnect between the growing recognition of young people as climate leaders and their limited access to financial resources. Discussions focused on legal and institutional eligibility requirements, limited climate finance literacy, complex application and compliance procedures, and a lack of accessible financing pathways for emerging youth-led initiatives.
Kazi Rawnaqul Islam, Managing Director of Bangladesh Climate Change Trust (BCCT), highlighted the Government of Bangladesh's commitment to supporting young climate leaders.
He said: “The Government of Bangladesh is willing and looking forward to investing in youth-led climate initiatives.”
Md Shamsuddoha, Chief Executive of Center for Participatory Research and Development (CPRD), emphasized the importance of consistency and differentiation for the sustainability of youth-led climate action.
He said: “Youth-led initiatives should demonstrate consistency, and their products and solutions must establish their own niche. This is essential for building credibility and long-term sustainability.”
Juel Mahmud, Liaison Officer in Bangladesh at the Green Climate Fund (GCF), underscored the need to strengthen young people's understanding of the climate finance landscape.
He said: “Young people must explore the different avenues of climate finance. Strengthening climate finance literacy should be a priority.”
Representing the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany in Dhaka, Jannis Hussain, Deputy Head of German Development Cooperation, encouraged young climate actors to approach financing opportunities with confidence.
He said: “Young people should not feel discouraged or afraid to seek financing to implement their ideas and initiatives.”
Farah Anzum, Bangladesh Lead at Global Strategic Communications Council (GSCC), called for greater institutional commitment to youth-led climate action.
She said: “Climate finance must move beyond promises and create real possibilities for young people. Stakeholders must place their trust in youth-led initiatives.”
A key highlight of the event was a presentation by Kamrul Hasan Shawon, Program Manager – Climate Change and Resilience (Portfolio Lead) at Plan International Bangladesh, titled “Youths in Climate Finance – What Does the Evidence and Practice Tell Us?”
The presentation examined climate finance through 3 interconnected perspectives: The Maze, The Mirror and The Bridge. It explored structural barriers within existing financing mechanisms, the need for young climate actors to strengthen their financial literacy and organizational readiness, and the importance of developing solutions that can be tested, sustained and scaled.
Drawing on practical examples from climate-adaptive agriculture, green enterprises and ecosystem-based adaptation, the discussion emphasized that youth-led climate action requires more than access to conventional grants.
Different solutions demand different financing approaches, including catalytic grants, enterprise financing, partnerships and appropriate intermediary support.
As a step toward addressing these challenges, Plan International Bangladesh announced its upcoming Flexible Funding Mechanism for Youth-Led Climate Solutions, with an official launch planned for early November 2026.
The proposed mechanism seeks to create a more accessible financing pathway for young climate actors, supporting the progression from promising ideas toward tested, sustainable and scalable climate solutions. Further details on its design, eligibility and application procedures will be shared during the official launch.
The event also featured an interactive Access–Barrier–Opportunity Dialogue, providing a platform for young participants and climate finance stakeholders to reflect on measures to improve financing accessibility, strengthen youth readiness and enable greater ownership of climate solutions.
The dialogue reinforced the message that meaningful youth participation in climate action must extend beyond representation in consultations and policy discussions. It requires accessible resources, institutional trust, appropriate financing instruments and sustained investment in young people's capacities to lead.
Through its engagement at RCOY APAC 2026, Plan International Bangladesh reaffirmed its commitment to advancing girls' and youth-led climate action and fostering partnerships that translate young people's climate ambitions into tangible and sustainable outcomes.

item.title: Verstappen wins Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
item.description:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his first win of the season at a chaotic Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Sunday that only started on the second attempt 1hr 40min late because of rain.
Verstappen gained the lead after an early safety car and led home the Mercedes of championship leader Kimi Antonelli and the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton at the Sepang International Circuit.
But there was agony for George Russell who had to retire from third place in the second Mercedes with five laps to go when his power unit appeared to fail under a late safety car.
An eventual standing start saw four-time world champion Verstappen start from pole for the first time this season after dominating practice and qualifying.
But he had a slow getaway on intermediate tyres allowing the Mercedes pair of Antonelli and Russell to pass him easily in the wet early conditions.
A safety car when Valtteri Bottas spun into the gravel on lap nine saw most drivers dive in for new slick tyres to take advantage of a rapidly drying track.
Verstappen took a lead that he would not relinquish when the safety car ended, swooping past Antonelli and Russell and quickly opened a comfortable gap.
Hamilton started on the front row on dry tyres and quickly slid down the field in the wet conditions.
But the seven-time world champion used all his experience to work his way back through the field for a brilliant podium place as the surface dried out.
His teammate Charles Leclerc was fourth with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar in fifth.
The Bahrain Grand Prix was being raced in Malaysia due to disruption in the Gulf linked to the US-led war with Iran.
Formula One moves on to nearby Singapore for a night race and sprint next weekend.

item.title: Asian Games close in Japan after records, rancour and rain
item.description:
The Asian Games in Japan closed on Sunday after a fortnight lit up by record-smashing young stars but marred by mishaps, mediocre crowds and accusations of mismanagement.
More than 17,000 athletes and officials, a bigger number than the Olympics, descended on Nagoya and Aichi prefecture for the continent's premier sporting spectacular.
Chinese swimming sensation Yu Zidi, just 13, stole the show with three gold medals, all in Games-record times.
She looks set to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
The schoolgirl was named a Games MVP to cap an extraordinary showing that saw her scorch to gold in the 200m butterfly and do the 200m-400m individual medley double.
For all that, the shy teenager said: "I don't think I am what people describe as a prodigy."
Also in the pool, Japanese swimmer Shin Ohashi, only 17, smashed the men's 200m breaststroke world record to delight the home crowd.
In athletics, where rain tumbled down over several days, the 20-year-old Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson did the 100m-200m double and was named men's MVP.
On a dry evening, a celebratory closing ceremony full of colour and song saw Japan hand over hosting duties to Doha 2030.
Top officials were on the defensive up until the last minute.
Olympic Council of Asia director general Husain Al-Musallam said "numbers are facts", pointing to 50 world records broken at the Games after they opened on September 19.
"The athletes cannot perform if they don't sleep good, the athletes cannot perform if they don't have good transportation," he said.
This 20th edition of the Games, which were first contested in 1951, did not have a traditional athletes' village in a bid to save money.
Instead, participants were housed in wooden temporary units, on cruise ship the Costa Serena and in hotels.
Organisers said this was a template for future multi-sports events.
But it came with issues, with some teams complaining the units were too cramped and the beds too short.
More than that, the ballooning numbers of athletes and officials meant there were not enough beds for everyone.
One Thai Olympic official told AFP it was "like musical chairs" trying to get somewhere to sleep.
The sport, including a blockbuster cricket final won by India against arch-rivals Pakistan, did sometimes shine through.
North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum, a 140cm (4ft 7in) pocket powerhouse, set three new world marks in one day for gold.
But problems kept coming, including organisers playing North Korea's national anthem for the South Korean hockey team.
There were athletes' buses that did not turn up when they should, or did not arrive at all.
Two teams were sent to the wrong venue, delaying a volleyball match.
"If I were to give them a grade, it would be an F," Ryu Seung-min, president of the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee, said.
Games organisers were on the back foot as well over attendances, with the opening ceremony taking place in front of thousands of empty seats.
At the women's football semi-final between hosts Japan and South Korea there were 998 spectators in a 50,000 stadium.
Japanese Olympic Committee president Seiko Hashimoto admitted that "there were many problems", but said the country wants to host more international events in future.
She said bad weather had turned some spectators off, but was eager to point out that some sports were well attended.
About 30,000 saw South Korea beat Japan 1-0 to clinch men's football gold, although the occasion was tarnished somewhat when the South Korean flag failed to go up in the victory ceremony.
The hosts finished with 83 golds, a distant second in the medals table behind China with 169.
Japan's tally included gold for Yuki Kurihara, who won an eSports competition aged 11, making him the youngest Games champion in history.
Several sports with ambitions of making the Olympics made their debut, including padel, MMA and virtual taekwondo.

item.title: Argentina hit Burkina Faso for seven ahead of Messi farewell
item.description:
Argentina produced another dominant attacking display, thrashing Burkina Faso 7-0 at the Monumental Stadium on Sunday to register back-to-back victories in their FIFA international friendlies ahead of Lionel Messi’s farewell appearance on home soil.
The emphatic victory followed Argentina’s 4-0 win over Bolivia, giving Lionel Scaloni’s side 11 goals across their last two matches without conceding.
Argentina took control from the outset, with Lautaro Martínez opening the scoring in the fourth minute after missing an initial penalty.
Agustín Giay was brought down inside the box by Moumouni Diallo, prompting the referee to point to the spot. Burkina Faso goalkeeper Razak Guira saved Martínez’s first attempt, but the Inter Milan striker reacted quickest to the rebound and fired home with his left foot.
Martínez, who also scored the opener against Bolivia, now has 42 goals in 86 international appearances, moving closer to Gabriel Batistuta’s Argentina record of 54 goals. Messi remains the country’s all-time leading scorer with 125.
Argentina doubled their advantage in the eighth minute when Diallo inadvertently turned the ball into his own net while attempting to clear.
Gianluca Prestianni made it 3-0 in the 12th minute, breaking into the penalty area before finishing powerfully for his first international goal.
The hosts continued to overwhelm their opponents, with Nicolás Paz adding the fourth in the 35th minute after making a well-timed run into space.
Julián Álvarez struck again just a minute later to cap a devastating first-half performance, sending Argentina into the break with a commanding 5-0 lead.
The attacking intensity remained undiminished after the interval, and substitute Franco Mastantuono made an immediate impact by scoring his first goal for the senior national team in the 57th minute.
The young attacker found himself one-on-one with Guira and calmly converted to make it 6-0, adding another memorable moment at the Monumental, where he had previously scored a spectacular free-kick for River Plate.
Burkina Faso struggled to contain Argentina throughout the contest, with the hosts continuing to create opportunities despite their overwhelming advantage.
Giovanni Simeone completed the rout in the third minute of stoppage time, finding the net in the 93rd minute to seal Argentina’s seventh goal.
The victory provided another confidence boost for the world champions as they prepare for Messi’s scheduled final appearance for Argentina at the Monumental on Tuesday against Benin.

item.title: Russia strikes hit Kyiv as Germany's Merz visits
item.description:
Russia struck another major bridge in Kyiv on Sunday, soon after Germany's chancellor arrived on a surprise visit to show European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks.
Air raid sirens blared repeatedly across the Ukrainian capital throughout the morning, including as Friedrich Merz met President Volodymyr Zelensky at the National Academy of Sciences, which was hit by a Russian attack drone on Monday.
Zelensky told him that people in Kyiv were suffering "terrible nights and days" from the relentless attacks, and called Ukraine's Russian adversaries "absolute barbarians".
"We can see the entire pointlessness of this war at this place," noted Merz.
"These barbarous attacks on the civilian population of Ukraine must stop. These are war crimes that are being committed daily here."
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said a strike had damaged the road surface on the Northern Bridge -- one of several connecting the eastern and western parts of the city over the Dnipro river which have been struck in repeatedly in the last four days.
Klitschko has said that Kyiv -- largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontlines in nearly five years of conflict -- should now be on a war footing due to the upsurge in attacks.
A spate of round-the-clock attacks has hit residential areas, petrol stations, schools, rail and communications infrastructure while near-constant air raid sirens disrupt daily life and put people on edge.
Merz said as he arrived that Ukraine "needs all our support in the coming weeks".
"If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us," he added.
Ukraine wants more Western military support, including advanced interceptors to shoot down Russia's new fast-moving, jet-powered drones.
On Sunday, Zelensky promised "important agreements". Government sources in Berlin said they were expected to shake hands on a new package of military support worth more than $1 billion.
It includes combat drones and satellite technology to help Ukraine hit Russian launch sites, as well as for the joint production of anti-jet drones, the German sources said.
"This support addresses the most significant current gap in Ukraine's air defence system. The impact is expected to be rapid and tangible," a source said.
Russia's defence ministry on Sunday vowed to ramp up its strikes on "military and military-industrial facilities" plus "related infrastructure in Kyiv" and elsewhere after Zelensky this week said Ukraine would intensify its own attacks against oil facilities that it says supply Moscow's troops.
Merz this week called for NATO and European unity against Russia as well as his own country, where the far-right, Moscow-friendly AfD opposition is on the rise.
There have been increasing fears in Europe that it could find itself in Russia's crosshairs.
Security was a top concern for voters in this weekend's election in NATO member Latvia, which borders Russia.
On Saturday, Moscow warned foreigners and diplomats to leave Kyiv, saying "massive" new airstrikes would hit the city.
It made a similar threat in May but leaders from Ukraine's allies have continued to make visits.
"The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!" EU ambassador Katarina Mathernova wrote on X on Sunday.
Mathernova told AFP separately that "nobody is moving", although European embassies always had contingency plans, including for winter, she added.
Russia has admitted deliberately targeting Ukraine's energy sector as winter approaches. Last year, similar attacks knocked out power and heating for days on end as temperatures plummeted to -20C.
In Kyiv, home to some three million people, residents are mulling what to do if that happens again, and there have been calls for the vulnerable and disabled to consider leaving.
Merz's trip was expected to announce some 350 million euros to help provide generators, transformer stations and for grid repairs, German government sources said.

item.title: Iran tells US there is no military solution to Middle East war
item.description:
Iran’s top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States’ war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.
A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.
The main point of contention remains Iran’s attempt to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, a vital conduit for Gulf oil and gas where a UK maritime agency reported on Sunday another tanker struck by an unknown projectile.
“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
“There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions,” he continued, adding “only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict.
The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June that spelled out a framework for a permanent resolution, but Iranian attacks on vessels in the Hormuz prompted a return to US military operations.
Iran has sought to impose its control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, striking vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.
The US has imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports, and has also struck vessels it accuses of violating it.
On Sunday, the British maritime security agency UKMTO said a tanker in the Hormuz “reported being struck by an unknown projectile, causing damage to the engine room”, though the crew were reported safe and no environmental impact was recorded.
The agency did not specify the date of the incident, the vessel’s origin or destination, or whether it was an oil tanker or LNG carrier.
Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.
Iran has demanded, among other things, a ceasefire across the Middle East, the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.
Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei on Sunday characterised the latest US counterproposal as being “in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues”.
“We have clearly indicated that we are focusing on the issue of the Strait of Hormuz,” he said, adding that reopening the waterway required “an end to the disruptions to Iranian commercial maritime traffic and the lifting of sanctions”.
The United States and Israel have characterised the war as being necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons -- a goal it has long denied pursuing -- though the focus soon shifted to reopening the Hormuz after its closure sent shockwaves through world energy markets.
The United States has not struck Iran since September 1, but it has recently pursued a fresh military buildup in the region.
