Air pollution has risen sharply across various parts of the country, including Dhaka. Today Dhaka ranked second among global cities with the worst air quality. However, pollution levels are even higher in areas surrounding the capital.

Air quality in Bangladesh generally improves during the monsoon, with the effects often lasting into autumn. But such severe air pollution during autumn is rarely observed.

At around 8:00am on Monday, Dhaka’s air quality index (AQI) stood at 185 on IQAir, a level classified as ‘unhealthy’. India’s capital New Delhi ranked ahead of Dhaka with an AQI of 308.

The figures were reported by Swiss-based IQAir, which regularly monitors and publishes air pollution data. Its live air quality index provides information and alerts people about how clean or polluted the air is in a particular city.

Air quality is particularly poor in areas surrounding Dhaka. According to IQAir, the AQI stood at 238 in Savar, 216 in Tongi and 191 in Gazipur.

The main sources of air pollution in Dhaka include emissions from unfit vehicles, dust from construction work and smoke from hundreds of brick kilns around the capital. Despite launching one project after another, the Department of Environment has failed to curb these sources of pollution. As a result, pollution levels have not declined.

Experts fear that air pollution could worsen further during the winter season this year.

item.title: Pritom– Shahtaj divorce, the couple shared reasons
item.description:
Musician and actor Pritom Hasan, and model, actress and singer Shahtaj Monira Hashem are ending their marriage. The couple has decided to go their separate ways due to some significant differences in their mutual understanding.

They announced the decision in separate Facebook posts on Sunday night. When contacted, Shahtaj confirmed the divorce to Prothom Alo.

In his post, Pritom wrote, “Shahtaj and I have mutually and amicably decided to end our marriage after ten years together.”

Pritom also expressed gratitude for the time they spent together. He wrote, “While we are grateful for the memories we shared and still care for each other, we realised over time that we are simply better off separate ways due to lack of mutual understanding.”

The musician also said that they did not make the decision suddenly. After much thought and discussion between themselves, and with the support and consent of their families, they reached the decision. They are currently going through the divorce process.

Shahtaj also shared a similar statement in her Facebook post. Alongside expressing gratitude for the time and memories they shared, she wrote that she would continue to hold respect and best wishes for Pritom.

Shahtaj said that, over time, they had realised that, due to some differences in their mutual understanding, it would be better for both of them to move forward separately. They made the decision with the support and consent of their families.

Both have requested that their privacy and personal space be respected during this period of change in their lives. They also requested their friends, colleagues and the media to treat the matter with respect and empathy. 

Pritom and Shahtaj first became acquainted and grew close while working together. Shahtaj appeared as a model in the music video for Pritom’s popular song “Jadukor”. They met while working on the song in 2017, and their relationship later developed into a romantic one.

After being in a long-term relationship, Pritom and Shahtaj married on 29 October 2022 at a hotel in Sreemangal, in the presence of members of both families and close friends.

Following their marriage, they shared moments from their life together on social media on various occasions. As recently as January this year, Pritom and Shahtaj were seen together at the wedding ceremony of musician Xefer Rahman and content creator Rafsan Sabab.

However, people close to the couple say that their relationship had not been going well for quite some time. There had also been discussions among those close to them about the possibility of their separation. Finally, both publicly announced that they had decided to end their marriage.

item.title: Messi readies for final farewell in Argentina send-off
item.description:
FILES-FBL-FRIENDLY-ARG-BEN

Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday (Bangladesh time Wednesday) with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions.

After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain's armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina's emerging generation.

Who will captain Argentina after Messi? Scaloni reveals the name

The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima.

Messi also bows out as Argentina's record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.

His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina's ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression.

"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.

Messi farewell match tickets sell out within two hours as website crashes

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

Friends reunited

Members of Argentina's 2022 World Cup-winning squad -- the players who delivered the country's third star -- and their families will join Messi for Tuesday's farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world.

Veterans of that Doha triumph such as Angel Di María, who retired from international football in 2024, will be there to witness the passing of the torch to a new generation charged with extending the Albiceleste's golden era.

Several of the newcomers, including Franco Mastantuono and Leonel Flores, were not even born when "La Pulga" ("The Flea") made his Argentina debut in 2005 for a team whose history had for so long been dominated by Diego Maradona.

"It's going to be an unforgettable day for everyone. Everyone wants to be at this match, and now it's just about enjoying it," Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said.

Argentina's new generation has already shown what it can do without its captain, although nobody is pretending replacing a man regarded by many as the greatest footballer in history will be straightforward.

"Collectively, we will try to fill the void left by Leo," said Scaloni, who is negotiating a contract extension after leaving his future unresolved following the World Cup defeat in July.

Scaloni, who mastered the art of building the right supporting cast around Messi, will also say goodbye on Tuesday to 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolas Otamendi.

Like Messi and Otamendi, midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up solely for the Benin game, raising the possibility that neither will represent Argentina again.

Argentina begin post-Messi era with 4-0 win over Bolivia

New generation

Those certain to be involved, at least from the bench, include other veterans of the 2022 World Cup who will be the standard-bearers for Argentina after Messi: defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez, and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.

Tenacious centre-back Romero is set to inherit the captain's armband, first worn by Messi at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Lautaro Martinez are next in the captaincy hierarchy.

They have already begun to rally around Messi's heirs, who showed their appetite for success in Argentina's first game since the World Cup final, against Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday.

Argentina swept the Bolivians aside 4-0, with young talents Nico Paz and Jose Manuel Lopez among the scorers.

They followed that victory with a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso at the Monumental on Saturday, with Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni scoring their first international goals.

While Argentina's future is beginning to take shape, one small but symbolically significant question remains: who inherits Messi's number 10 shirt?

"We won't give the number 10 to anyone until Leo's match takes place," Scaloni said. "After that, we'll see."

item.title: Tk 650 knife bought on whim, murdered a rickshaw puller on birthday night
item.description:
The 16-year-old boy had bought the knife from a footpath vendor for Tk 650. He was so excited about the item he had bought that he called over friends to show it to them. A few days later, on the night of his birthday, that same knife claimed the life of a rickshaw puller.

There was no record of the teenager being involved in any crime before. Police also found no such history involving the two friends who were with him. Yet, over the course of a few hours on one night, the lives of all three teenagers became entangled in a murder case.

It all started with a birthday party. Then came his first experience of drinking alcohol, roaming around with friends late at night, a minor argument with a rickshaw puller, encouragement from another friend, a slap and finally, a single strike with the newly bought knife. This chain of events emerged from an investigation by the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.

The murder took place in the early hours of last Wednesday in the Gabtoli area of Darussalam in the capital. The Mirpur Division of DB arrested the three teenagers involved in the incident on Saturday. One of them had just turned 16, while the other two were under 15.

The incident comes at a time when concerns over crime and violence involving teenagers have resurfaced. Two widely discussed murders involving teenagers took place in Cumilla and Chattogram in the past few weeks. Drives against teen gangs are also underway in various districts.

According to police, as many as 127 teen gangs or subgroups have been identified in Dhaka alone. Police Headquarters recently issued directives to gather field-level information on teen gangs and their patrons.

But the Gabtoli incident is different as the police have so far found no link to any organised gang. The incident therefore highlights not only the issue of teen gangs but also how easily risks such as weapons, substance use, late-night hangouts and peer pressure can enter the lives of ordinary teenagers.

Days After Buying the Knife

According to DB sources, the teenager named Saad (pseudonym) had purchased a knife from a footpath vendor for Tk 650 out of curiosity a few days earlier. Investigation sources said Saad was quite thrilled after buying the knife. He called several friends over to show it to them and carried it with him whenever he went out.

Saad turned 16 on 30 September. On the occasion of his birthday, an older acquaintance named Ruel invited him to a party. Saad told investigators that he drank alcohol for the first time in his life at that party.

After the party ended around 1:00am, Saad went to the Gabtoli area. He then called his friend Farid (pseudonym) and asked him to come out of his home. Saying that he wanted to go out at night to celebrate his birthday, Saad took him along.

The two were walking around Gabtoli when a cycle rickshaw passed by them. Initially, the two teenagers suspected the rickshaw puller of being a mugger based on his behaviour. Although they later realised that was not the case, they got into an argument with him.

At one point, the rickshaw puller left the place. The incident could have ended there but it did not.

Another friend arrives, the puller reappears

Around 3:00am, Saad and Farid called another friend, Zahid (pseudonym) and asked him to come outside. Zahid initially did not want to go out. He eventually left home after learning that it was Saad’s birthday

The three friends sat down at a tea stall next to Allah'r Daan Hotel in Gabtoli. During their conversation, they brought up the earlier argument with the rickshaw puller.

According to investigators, after hearing what had happened, Zahid encouraged his friends to beat up the rickshaw puller if they came across him again. Shortly afterwards, the three teenagers saw the rickshaw puller again.

According to DB sources, Saad and Zahid got into another argument with him as soon as they saw him. At one point, the rickshaw puller got off the rickshaw and entered Allah’r Dan Hotel nearby. The teenagers assumed that he had gone inside the hotel to complain about them. This made them even more angry.

A short while later, when the rickshaw puller came out of the hotel, Zahid slapped him. Immediately afterwards, Saad took out the Tk 650 knife he was carrying and struck the rickshaw puller on the back of his neck.

Investigators said the entire incident took place within a short period of time.

Attempting to flee with that rickshaw

After being stabbed, the injured rickshaw puller climbed onto his rickshaw and tried to flee the scene. But after traveling a short distance, he collapsed onto the vehicle. Moments later, he died there. The three teenagers also fled the area.

Mohammad Rakib Khan, deputy commissioner of the DB-Mirpur division, told Prothom Alo that none of the three teenagers had any prior criminal record, nor were they professional criminals. Based on investigation findings, he said they became involved in the murder driven by impulsiveness, spontaneous reaction and peer provocation.

One night, several risk factors

Experts say multiple risk factors converged in the Gabtoli incident. Buying and carrying a knife out of hobby, consuming alcohol for the first time on a birthday, teenagers staying out late at night and peer provocation. A minor dispute escalated rapidly into violence and ultimately that knife was used in the murder.

Professor Fatema Rezina Iqbal of the Department of Sociology at the University of Dhaka told Prothom Alo that teenagers do not possess fully developed emotional regulation skills. As a result, in many instances they may become drawn towards crime or teenage gang culture.

Fatema Rezina Iqbal stressed the importance of parental supervision in such cases. She said parents need to keep track of when their children go out, where they go and whom they spend time with. Such ways of celebrating birthdays or occasions that bring teenagers together can increase their tendency towards crime. Such incidents are a matter of concern for society, she added.

Three teenagers caught on CCTV

The Detective Branch is investigating the murder case filed at Darussalam Police Station over the killing of the rickshaw puller in Gabtoli. Investigators began identifying those involved the day after the killing. By analysing CCTV footage from Allah'r Daan Hotel and surrounding areas, they identified images of the three teenagers.

Initially, detectives suspected that professional muggers might have been involved in the killing. Three suspected muggers were taken into custody and interrogated on that suspicion. However, the investigation found that none of them was involved in the killing.

Later, they were shown pictures of the suspects obtained from CCTV footage. One of them recognized Farid, as Farid used to work at a hotel in the Gabtoli area. Subsequently, Farid was first taken into DB custody from Jatrabari in Dhaka. Based on information provided by him, DB picked up Zahid from Bhola and Saad from Nabinagar in Brahmanbaria.

The victim’s name remains unknown

While investigators managed to identify the three teenagers through CCTV footage, police have yet to discover the name of the rickshaw puller whose death sparked the entire investigation. He was approximately 20 years old.

Police sources revealed that the young man had arrived in Dhaka from Pabna about a month ago. He rented a cycle-rickshaw from a garage in the Darussalam area to earn a living. However, he did not return to the garage regularly and spent some nights outside.

Even with assistance from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), the DB could not identify the deceased youth.

Darussalam police had earlier sought the public's help in identifying him. Ever since his death, his body has been lying in the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College.

Dulal Hossain, Officer-in-Charge of Darussalam Police Station, told Prothom Alo that they suspect the young man did not have a National Identity Card (NID). Once his identity is confirmed, the body will be handed over to his family.

For the man lying in the morgue, the only thing left to wait for now is the confirmation of his identity. The family of the young man, who came to Dhaka from Pabna a few weeks ago in search of a livelihood, may not yet even know that he will never return.

item.title: Planned in afternoon, attack at night, 2 gangs supplied men
item.description:
A dispute over land and an access road culminated in a calculated plot to attack a housing project—hatched inside a local eatery and executed at night by hired operatives from two criminal gangs.

According to investigative sources, this armed assault on the New Gini Housing Project near ECB Chattar in the capital unfolded following a meeting in the afternoon and a subsequent gathering later in the day.

Sources said that following the afternoon strategy meeting, assailants gathered at two distinct locations. Approximately 200 attackers made their way to the site on foot and aboard five pickup trucks. At around 10:30 pm, the group launched their attack by opening fire at the main gate.

The attackers comprised members of criminal groups led by Ibrahim and Mamun from Mirpur in the capital. Ibrahim, the convener of the Bhasantek Thana unit BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party), is listed in police records as ‘Killer Ibrahim’.

The planning meeting took place in the afternoon inside an eatery near ECB Circle. By 4:00 pm, one group gathered in the field opposite the Dewanpara Two-Storey Mosque in Bhasantek, while another assembled in the Manikdi area.

Sources involved with the investigation state that armed with firearms and wooden batons, around 200 men travelled from those gathering points to the New Gini Housing Project via five pickup trucks and on foot. At approximately 10:30 pm, they breached the project by opening fire at the entrance.

Investigation sources indicate that operatives from two Mirpur-based criminal gangs took part in the attack. One faction is headed by Ibrahim, convener of the Bhasantek Thana unit BNP, and the other by Mofizur Rahman Mamun of Pallabi.

Ibrahim’s loyalists constituted the majority of the force. A contractor named Bikash Chandra Shah was entrusted with the task of recruiting men from both gangs.

During the assault on the New Gini Properties housing project on the night of 26 September, assailants also vandalised and ransacked the studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir, located within the premises. Later that night, Salman released a video detailing the incident, triggering widespread outrage across social media and public platforms.

Police have so far arrested seven individuals in connection with the attack and vandalism. The detainees include Major General (retd) Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury, Mizanur Rahman, Shahriar Mahmud, Shah Alam, Mamun, Aslam, and Munna. The fourth named accused, Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury, was the latest to be apprehended on Wednesday.

Police confirmed that all seven suspects are currently in remand. It has been clarified that the arrested suspect Mamun and gang leader Mofizur Rahman Mamun are two different individuals.

The investigation has been transferred from Cantonment police station to the Gulshan Division of the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.

AFM Anwar Hossain, Deputy Commissioner of DB Gulshan Division, informed Prothom Alo that the attack stemmed from a land dispute.

He confirmed seven arrests to date and stated that efforts are underway to apprehend the remaining suspects. He added that investigations are ongoing on who orchestrated the plot, participated in the assault, and supplied the arms, with gathered intelligence currently undergoing verification.

Strategy meeting at the eatery

Multiple officers involved in the investigation told Prothom Alo that a planning meeting took place in an eatery near ECB Chattar in the afternoon. CCTV footage from the establishment captured 13 individuals present, two of whom have been identified: the arrested suspect Shahriar Mahmud and contractor Bikash Chandra Shah.

Investigation sources indicate that operatives from two Mirpur-based criminal gangs took part in the attack. One faction is headed by Md. Ibrahim, convener of the Bhasantek Thana unit BNP, and the other by Mofizur Rahman Mamun of Pallabi.

They said efforts were ongoing to identify the remaining 11 individuals. Investigators confirmed that the meeting served as the primary forum for planning the assault, with both Shahriar and Bikash actively involved.

Further inquiries revealed that Bikash works as a building construction contractor across various housing projects. A dispute over land had been brewing between Nazim Uddin Bhuiyan, the owner of the New Gini Housing Project, and several individuals including Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury. Bikash had been awarded the contract to construct a building on the disputed land.

Investigative sources claim Bikash was tasked not only with construction but also with negotiating an access road with the owner of New Gini. However, Nazim Uddin refused to grant access—a refusal investigators believe served as the direct catalyst for the attack.

Bikash Chandra Shah could not be reached for comment regarding his alleged role in the planning and recruitment of assailants, as he remains in hiding. Police stated that operations are underway to trace and arrest him.

Mobilisation from 2 gangs

According to investigative sources, the decision to strike was finalised during the eatery meeting, with Bikash assigned the task of gathering the manpower. Bikash reportedly reached out to Ibrahim and Mofizur Rahman Mamun through Shah Alam Onik, joint convener of the Muktijoddha Projonmo League. Operatives from both groups were subsequently deployed as hired mercenaries.

Several residents of the Dewanpara area in Bhasantek told Prothom Alo that Ibrahim maintains a business office opposite the Two-Storey Mosque. At around 4:00 pm on the day of the incident, men brought in from the Bhasantek slum and Pallabi gathered in the field in front of the mosque.

Local residents alleged that Masum alias ‘Forsa Masum’, a key lieutenant of Ibrahim’s gang, rounded up the attackers and led them to the New Gini Housing Project.

Mofizur Rahman Mamun previously served as the president of ward no. 91 BNP under Pallabi Thana. He was expelled from the party on Tuesday following allegations of murder, land grabbing, extortion, and other criminal acts.

Investigative sources noted that a significant portion of the attackers came from the Bhasantek slum. Two individuals arrested at the scene with firearms were also residents of the area and confirmed loyalists of Ibrahim.

A police source claimed that Ibrahim’s followers—including Juboraj, Shahed, Shakil, Rupchan, Bablu, and Bukpora Sumon—were directly involved in the attack. All of them face prior allegations of involvement in various criminal activities across Bhasantek.

Locals further alleged that Ibrahim’s operatives routinely descend upon any prospective building site in Bhasantek, forcing developers to hire their earth-filling services and purchase construction materials—such as bricks, sand, and cement—exclusively through them.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, a property owner told Prothom Alo that Ibrahim’s men had approached him demanding he buy materials from them. When he declined, they opened fire outside his under-construction property, ultimately forcing him to purchase sub-standard bricks and sand from Ibrahim.

Police confirmed that operatives belonging to Mofizur Rahman Mamun’s gang in Pallabi also participated in the attack on New Gini.

According to the law enforcement, members of this gang operate as hired muscle to forcibly clear and seize land across Mirpur and adjoining areas, and are implicated in numerous criminal activities across Mirpur and Pallabi.

Mofizur Rahman Mamun previously served as the president of Ward No. 91 BNP under Pallabi Thana. He was expelled from the party on Tuesday following allegations of murder, land grabbing, extortion, and other criminal acts.

Nazim Uddin Bhuiyan, owner of the New Gini Housing Project, also confirmed to Prothom Alo that operatives from both Ibrahim and Mamun’s gangs were directly involved in the attack on his property.

Attempts were made to contact Ibrahim and Mofizur Rahman Mamun via telephone to obtain their responses to the allegations of dispatching armed goons, but neither could be reached.

Gunfire directed at police

As the violence escalated, six police members arrived at the scene. Investigative sources stated that the assailants fired directly at the responding officers. The identities of those who opened fire on the police, as well as other armed attackers present during the attack, are yet to be established.

The First Information Report (FIR) filed in connection with the case alleges that approximately 50 rounds were fired by the attackers during the attack. Police, on the other hand, stated that they fired five rounds of bullets to bring the situation under control.

Nazim Uddin told Prothom Alo that Golam Mohiuddin had sold 15 kathas out of the 35-katha plot to him. Nazim had subsequently filled the land with soil and erected a boundary wall, which was demolished by attackers following the political shifts on 5 August 2024.

Efforts were made to reach content creator Salman Muqtadir for his account of the attack on his studio and his complaint, but he was unavailable for comment.

Meanwhile, on Wednesday, the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) requested Salman Muqtadir’s bank account details and transaction histories, acting on information provided by an intelligence agency.

Disputed land and access road

Nazim Uddin Bhuiyan launched his real estate business in the ECB Chattar area under Cantonment police station in 2011. His New Gini Housing Project currently spans an area of 10 to 12 bighas.

The investigation highlighted an ongoing dispute over an adjacent 35-katha plot of land. A visit to the location on Friday revealed the plot without any construction, bordered on three sides by local residential dwellings and on the fourth by the New Gini Housing Project. The central point of contention involves using the internal road of the New Gini project as an exit route for that land.

Nazim Uddin told Prothom Alo that Golam Mohiuddin had sold 15 kathas out of the 35-katha plot to him. Nazim had subsequently filled the land with soil and erected a boundary wall, which was demolished by attackers following the political shifts on 5 August 2024.

Nazim alleged that Golam Mohiuddin, without handing over possession of the land, publicly announced plans to construct a high-rise building on the site while demanding an access road through the New Gini Housing Project. When Nazim refused to grant access, Mohiuddin deployed hired goons to carry out the attack.

Cases against Nazim too

The owner of New Gini, Nazim Uddin, faces land-related allegations of his own. In July, a man named Mizanur Rahman filed a lawsuit against Nazim at Cantonment police station, accusing him of selling an eight-and-a-half-katha plot in Joar Sahara to a third party without paying the full purchase price.

According to the case statement, a deed of agreement (Bayana) was executed in 2024 for the land at a price of Tk 54 million. Nazim paid an initial instalment of Tk 10 million, with the remaining Tk 44 million due within five months. The plaintiff alleges that Nazim defaulted on the payment and instead sold the land to another buyer.

Addressing allegations of using political influence to grab land during the Awami League administration, Nazim Uddin claimed that business rivals had repeatedly harassed him by falsely aligning him with various political factions.

He stated that in 2022, he was arrested and imprisoned under the Special Powers Act across multiple police stations in Dhaka on false charges of ties to the BNP and Jamaat.

He further noted that cases were filed against him at Cantonment police station during the July mass uprising, and following 5 August 2024, his adversaries have continued to target him by labeling him a ‘collaborator of the Awami League’.

Every climate shock is putting girls at risk: Study
item.description:
Climate disasters are driving greater risks of child marriage, teenage pregnancy, and violence for girls, according to a new global research by Plan International.

The study combines a large-scale analysis of health and climate data spanning more than 50 countries over three decades with a survey of 5,000 girls, in-depth interviews and focus group discussions with 139 girls, across Bangladesh, Kenya, Peru, Senegal, and Zimbabwe, says a press release.

The study found that climate disasters such as floods, droughts, cyclones, and extreme heat are destroying the health and education services girls depend on at the precise moment they need them most, with the consequences falling hardest on girls who already have the least.

Key findings of the report include:

One in 10 girls said they had personally experienced an unintended pregnancy following a climate-related event, while 33 per cent reported an increase in unintended pregnancies in their community.

One in 10 girls said they had personally married before the age of 18, and 36 per cent reported seeing more girls married or in a union before they turned 18 in their community following climate-related disasters.

More than a quarter (28 per cent) of girls said they had observed an increase in violence against women and girls following climate-related events.

Nine in 10 girls said climate-related events were placing serious pressure on their family's survival, health, and stability.

More than three-quarters (76 per cent) of girls said more girls and young women in their community were struggling to access at least one health service, rising to 84 per cent among those affected by drought.

Girls from minority communities were twice as likely to struggle to access services, nearly three times as likely to report an unintended pregnancy, and more than twice as likely to face pressure to marry young.

Behind many of these consequences lies a simple but devastating reality: climate shocks are pulling girls out of school. When education is disrupted, girls lose the single most protective factor in their lives, making them significantly more vulnerable to exploitation, violence, early marriage, and lost access to health services.

"For girls, the climate crisis is not a distant threat. It is already disrupting their education and increasing the risks they face when they cannot access health services. Only half of national climate plans mention girls’ or women’s health, and despite the escalating impact of climate shocks on the health systems and services girls rely on, just 0.5 per cent of multilateral climate finance supports health", said Reena Ghelani, Plan International CEO.

Girls reported increased risks of sexual exploitation in the aftermath of climate shocks, including being pressured into exchanging sex for money or basic necessities as protection systems and support networks break down.

Girls also reported heightened danger in emergency shelters, where cramped conditions and darkness left them exposed to harassment and sexual violence.

"When floods leave people completely destitute, families think about financial hardship and marry off girls at a very young age," said Shahina, 19, from Bangladesh. Participants in the study described girls becoming pregnant from as young as 12 and 13 in Peru, with girls in Zimbabwe noting pregnancy among girls still in primary and early secondary school.

Almost half of girls (49 per cent) noticed more pregnancy health or childbirth related complications, including miscarriages, in their community following a climate shock. Nearly one in four said access to healthcare during pregnancy and delivery care became harder to reach.

The research also identifies a form of climate harm that is almost entirely absent from disaster planning. Slow-onset drought destroys the household economies that keep girls out of marriage.

Across 52 countries and three decades, prolonged drought emerged as the hazard most consistently associated with rising rates of child marriage and early unions, as families lose harvests, livestock, and income over months and years until marrying a daughter becomes a survival strategy.

"My father has no livestock to sell and take me to college, that's how I accepted to be married off," said Galgalo, a 22-year-old participant from Kenya.

Because slow-onset drought rarely triggers an emergency response, this damage accumulates unseen. Girls whose schooling was disrupted were twice as likely to marry young or face an unintended pregnancy. A secondary analysis spanning over 50 countries across three decades confirmed that uninterrupted education is the single most consistent protective factor against early marriage and violence.

The findings highlight how climate-related disasters are exacerbating existing inequalities and vulnerabilities for girls, increasing risks to their health, safety, and wellbeing. This year, the El Niño weather pattern is intensifying weather extremes across the globe and predictions expect it to be the most powerful in decades.

In Peru, girls described how recurring El Niño floods disrupted access to health services, cut off transport routes, and increased pressure on already struggling families. With El Niño conditions projected to intensify further in the coming months, the window to act before these impacts deepen is narrowing.

With the world's attention soon to turn to COP31, where countries have an opportunity to negotiate international action on climate change Plan International is calling on governments and donors to act:

Keep schools open and free during climate shocks - education is the single most consistent protective factor across three decades of data, and girls whose schooling is disrupted are twice as likely to marry young or face an unintended pregnancy.

Allocate a defined share of climate adaptation finance to adolescent girls' health, including sexual and reproductive health services, contraception, and maternity care.

Include menstrual products, contraception, and protection services in every emergency response package, not as a later stage intervention

Reach the most marginalised girls. Girls from minority communities, those with disabilities, and those already displaced face the greatest barriers and receive the least support.

“We know what puts girls at risk, and we know what helps protect them. What is missing is not the evidence, but the urgency to act on it. Girls cannot continue to be treated as an afterthought in climate action. They must have a meaningful say in the decisions that shape their lives, and their rights and needs must be built into climate policy and financing from the outset”, said Reena Ghelani.

item.title: New Gini attack: Retired major general Mohiuddin secures bail
item.description:
A court has granted bail to former army officer Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury in a case filed over vandalism, looting and theft at the ‘New Gini Properties Limited’ housing project in the capital’s ECB Chattar area.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate (DMP) Aminul Islam Junaid granted him bail on Sunday after a hearing, on a Tk 2,000 bond. Tarek Rahman, sub-inspector of the DMP’s prosecution division, confirmed the matter to Prothom Alo on Monday.

He said the accused’s lawyers applied for bail after the remand ended on Sunday, and the court granted the application.

Planned in afternoon, attack at night, 2 gangs supplied men

According to court sources, Mohiuddin was produced before the court on Sunday after a three-day remand. On the same day, the case’s investigating officer and Detective Branch (DB) Inspector Jehad Hossain sought an order to keep him in jail.

At that point, Dhaka Bar Association General Secretary Mohammad Abul Kalam Khan sought bail on behalf of the accused. Following the hearing, the court granted bail until 28 October. No lawyer representing the prosecution was present at the hearing.

Mohiuddin was arrested from a house in Segunbagicha under Ramna police station on 30 September. The following day, 1 October, the court put him on three days’ remand.

Attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio: ‘Vandals entered New Gini Properties firing shots’

Around midnight on 26 September, a group of people armed with weapons attacked the housing project of New Gini Properties Limited in the capital’s ECB Chattar area. They fired around 50 shots indiscriminately and carried out an attack with machetes, knives and sticks.

At one point, the attackers entered the studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir and carried out extensive vandalism. They also looted various items from the studio. That night, Salman Muqtadir posted a video on social media showing his vandalised studio, sparking widespread discussion across the country.

In connection with the incident, project official Saiful Islam Bhuiyan filed a case with Cantonment police station. The case names 13 people as accused and includes another 150 to 200 unidentified people.

item.title: Deepto TV executive murder case: Court rejects plea to implicate minister Rabiul, 8 others
item.description:
A Dhaka court has rejected a petition seeking to implicate Road Transport Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam and eight others in the murder case of Deepto TV broadcast executive Tanzil Jahan Tamim in the capital’s Hatirjheel area.

The order was passed today, Monday, by Dhaka’s 13th Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Zahidul Islam after hearing the petition.

Court Bench Assistant Sohel Mia confirmed the matter, saying the nine individuals had earlier been discharged from the case. The complainant subsequently filed a revision petition challenging their discharge. The court has now rejected that petition, he said.

“The case will proceed against those who have been charge-sheeted,” Sohel Mia said.

Expressing dissatisfaction with the order, Abdul Alim, counsel for the complainant, said, “We are not satisfied with the order. We will move the High Court against it.”

Tamim was attacked at his home in the Mahanagar residential area of Hatirjheel on 10 October 2024. He was taken to hospital in critical condition, where physicians declared him dead. The following day, his father, Sultan Ahmed, filed a murder case with Hatirjheel police station.

The case named 16 people, including Mirza Abdul Latif, managing director of developer company Pleasant Properties; BNP Central Executive Committee member Sheikh Rabiul Alam; and Mohammad Mamun, deputy director of the Department of Narcotics Control. Eleven to 12 unidentified people were also named as accused.

On the day the case was filed, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) said at a press conference that Pleasant Properties, owned by Sheikh Rabiul Alam, had constructed a building on Tamim’s father’s land under an agreement. A dispute over the distribution of flats in the building had led to allegations that Mamun, a representative of the developer company, and several others beat Tamim to death.

Following its investigation, the Dhaka North unit of the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) submitted a charge sheet against 13 people and a delinquency report against a juvenile to the court on 10 December 2025. However, it recommended that nine people, including Rabiul Alam, be discharged for lack of “specific evidence” against them.

Dissatisfied with the recommendation, Tamim’s father Sultan Ahmed filed a no-objection petition with the court on 8 January.

On 3 March, Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Awlad Hossain Mohammad Junaid rejected the complainant’s petition and accepted the charge sheet in the case. He also discharged Rabiul Alam and the other eight from the case.

The 13 people against whom the charge sheet has been accepted are Pleasant Properties Ltd. Managing Director Mirza Abdul Latif, CEO Faizul Ahmed alias Suman, Mamunur Rashid Mamun, Korban Ali, SM Ibrahim Hossain, Badhan, Gazi Zakir Hossain, Russel, Monir Hossain, Shahraj Uddin, Amirul Islam alias Amir, Suman Mallik and Mahfuzar Rahman.

Those discharged from the case are Department of Narcotics Control Deputy Director Mohammad Mamun, Sheikh Rabiul Alam, Fazlur Rahman, Arian, Nasrin Akter, Russel, Mahfuzur Rahman, Mozammel Haque Kabir and Imam Hossain.

Sultan Ahmed filed the revision petition challenging their discharge.

item.title: Battery-powered rickshaw drivers block road in front of Press Club for an hour
item.description:
Battery-powered rickshaw drivers staged a protest and blocked the road in front of the National Press Club in the capital on Monday.

They initially gathered in Paltan at around 11:00 am before blocking the road in front of the National Press Club. The road remained closed to traffic for an hour.

According to eyewitnesses and police, the protesting drivers forced several passengers to get out of the rickshaws during the blockade, causing them inconvenience.

Police said the rickshaw drivers were protesting and blocked the road over several demands. The drivers demanded that battery-powered rickshaws charged using legal electricity connections not be disconnected. They also demanded that illegal connections not be disconnected.

Meanwhile, four rickshaw drivers were detained several days ago and sent to jail through executive magistrates. The protesting drivers also demanded their release.

Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of police in the Ramna division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), told Prothom Alo at noon that the rickshaw drivers had gathered there over several demands.

He further said police later went to the scene and brought the situation under control. Traffic is now moving normally.

item.title: No compromise on airport security: Civil aviation minister
item.description:
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat has said there will be no compromise whatsoever when it comes to airport security. He said the first few minutes are crucial if a fire or any other accident occurs at an airport, and the response time in emergencies must be reduced further.

The minister made the remarks today, Monday, after the ‘Airport Emergency Exercise (Fire)-2026’ drill at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka.

Rashiduzzaman Millat said fire safety and emergency response capabilities are key foundations for establishing a modern and secure aviation hub.

During a fire, immediate communication and coordination must be ensured among the Fire Service, airport authorities, operations and security teams, medical teams and other relevant agencies.

The minister said initiatives had been taken to sign memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with the relevant ministries and agencies to strengthen emergency response.

Referring to the fire at the airport’s import cargo complex last October, Rashiduzzaman Millat said the incident caused substantial damage and harmed the country’s image. Ensuring security is therefore the highest priority of the current government, he said.

The minister said that after taking office, the government had formed a National Civil Aviation Security Committee to strengthen security in the sector. An audit by the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) will be conducted soon, he said, adding that measures had been taken to ensure compliance with issues that may be identified during the audit.

Rashiduzzaman Millat said no special security concessions would be given to VIPs or CIPs at the airport. Security protocols have been kept the same for everyone, he said, adding that everyone must follow those protocols to ensure airport security.

The minister said an initiative had been taken to install a comprehensive anti-drone system to prevent unauthorised drone flights.

He said the airport is a critical state facility and unauthorised drones had even been seen flying during the fire. A comprehensive anti-drone system will therefore be installed to prevent unauthorised drone flights in the airport area.

Rashiduzzaman Millat stressed the need to maintain an adequate number of security-related equipment at the airport, particularly scanners. He said it was the responsibility of everyone concerned to ensure passengers can travel safely, smoothly and comfortably.

The minister stressed the importance of implementing recommendations arising from the drill. He said emergency management capabilities must be further strengthened by implementing the recommendations that emerge from the post-drill assessment. Regular, realistic drills would improve the ability to respond quickly and effectively to emergencies, he said.

Punishment for Negligence

In response to questions from journalists after the drill, Rashiduzzaman Millat said the government had taken a strict stance against negligence of duty at the airport. He said the current government was a government of the people. Anyone who neglects their responsibilities would be punished, while those who perform their duties properly would be rewarded.

Asked about various allegations of passenger harassment and disorder at the airport recently, the minister said the authorities were taking steps to address the incidents that had occurred.

However, he said some misinformation was also being spread.

Asked about a woman’s allegation of harassment, Rashiduzzaman Millat said he had immediately looked into the matter. There was no truth to the incident as described, he said.

Addressing journalists, the minister urged them to inform the authorities if they came across genuine incidents. At the same time, he said, the truth must be reported and the spread of false information must be prevented.

In his closing remarks at the drill, Rashiduzzaman Millat said the government was committed to making the country’s civil aviation sector more modern, safe and up to international standards, with passenger safety and service receiving the highest priority. The collective efforts of all relevant institutions and agencies would continue towards achieving this goal.

Bangladesh Civil Aviation Authority (CAAB) Chairman Air Vice Marshal Md Mostofa Mahmood Siddiq and Dhaka-18 MP SM Jahangir Hossain also spoke at the event.
